setupSteps: Check the machine. Look at the placard. On a combo pec deck, set the arms to the reverse (rear-delt) position or turn to face the pad if the machine is designed that way. Make sure nothing is under the stack.

Choose the handle grip. Neutral (palms facing each other) is the FitPlate default because Schoenfeld 2013 found slightly higher rear-delt and infraspinatus activity; palms-down is fine if it feels better.
Select the load. Put the weight-stack pin in a very light plate (about 15-25 percent of what you would use on the pec deck, est.) and push the pin all the way in.

Seat height: set the seat so that when your arms are held out in front of you, the handles are at about shoulder level and your arms are roughly parallel to the floor (est.). Sources vary: shoulder height, arms parallel to the floor, or handles in front of the shoulders. Handles at the ears or down by the stomach change the pull angle and shift work to the traps or front delts.
Chest against the pad: sit facing the machine with the chest (not the belly) against the pad, head upright, shoulders away from your ears. Do not pull your chest off the pad during the set.
Feet: flat on the floor or the foot bar, hip-width apart.

Starting handle position: pull the handles in front of you (use the range-limiter or start-position lever if the machine has one) so your arms start about in front of the chest, hands near each other, not touching.
Elbows: slightly bent (about 150-170 degrees, est.) and keep that bend through the whole rep. Hands and wrists stay in line with the forearms.
Brace and breathe. Sit tall, ribs down, belly lightly tight.

steps.title: Sit and set your chest
steps.action: Sit facing the pad with your chest touching it and your feet flat.
steps.feel: Chest and upper stomach supported by the pad.
steps.visualCheck: Side: head over the shoulders, chest on the pad. Front: shoulders level.

steps.title: Take the handles
steps.action: Hold both handles with a neutral or palms-down grip, thumbs wrapped, arms in front of you at about shoulder height.
steps.feel: A light stretch across the back of the shoulders.
steps.visualCheck: Front: both handles at the same height; elbows slightly bent.

steps.title: Set the shoulders down
steps.action: Gently lower your shoulders away from your ears.
steps.visualCheck: Front: shoulders low, not touching ears.

steps.title: Sweep the arms back
steps.action: Lead with the elbows, sweeping the handles out and back in a wide arc, keeping the elbow bend the same.
steps.feel: The back of the shoulders working, not the neck or the lower back.
steps.visualCheck: Front or top-three-quarter: both arms move out evenly; elbows stay slightly bent.

steps.title: Finish at about the shoulder line
steps.action: Stop when your arms are about in line with your shoulders (hands roughly level with the chest and elbows pointing out); do not go far behind the shoulder line.
steps.feel: A small squeeze between the shoulder blades, gentle only.
steps.visualCheck: Top view: arms about in a straight line across the shoulders; no shrug.

steps.title: Hold briefly
steps.visualCheck: Chest still on the pad; torso not swinging.

steps.title: Return slowly
steps.action: Let the handles come back in front of you in the same arc, controlling the stack.
steps.visualCheck: Both handles return together; the stack does not drop or touch hard.

steps.title: Finish the set
steps.action: After the last rep, bring the handles slowly to the start and let go.
steps.visualCheck: Both hands off together; stack at rest.

commonMistakes.title: Weight too heavy
commonMistakes.text: Weight too heavy. Why: the upper traps and back muscles take over and the rear delt does little (most-cited mistake in the sources). Fix: choose a load that lets you pause for one second at the end of every rep.

commonMistakes.title: Shrugging
commonMistakes.text: Shrugging. Why: shifts work to the upper traps and can strain the neck. Fix: shoulders down, use less weight.

commonMistakes.title: Swinging the torso or using momentum
commonMistakes.text: Swinging the torso or using momentum. Why: removes tension from the rear shoulder (coaches call momentum the biggest error on this machine). Fix: chest on the pad, 2 s out, 3 s back.

commonMistakes.title: Pulling far behind the shoulder line
commonMistakes.text: Pulling far behind the shoulder line. Why: the traps and rhomboids take over and the front of the shoulder can be stretched under load (BarBend and others say limit range if the rear delt is not feeling it). Fix: stop when arms are about level with the shoulders.

commonMistakes.title: Seat too low or too high
commonMistakes.text: Seat too low or too high. Why: a low seat turns it into a high pull with shrugging; a high or low handle changes the pull angle and can recruit the front delts. Fix: handles at about shoulder level.

commonMistakes.title: Bending or straightening the elbows during the rep
commonMistakes.text: Bending or straightening the elbows during the rep. Why: turns it into a row or a locked-elbow lever, loading the elbows. Fix: keep a soft elbow bend, the same throughout.

commonMistakes.title: Chest off the pad or arching the lower back
commonMistakes.text: Chest off the pad or arching the lower back. Why: shifts work away from the rear delt and strains the lower back. Fix: chest against the pad, ribs down.

commonMistakes.title: Half-inserted pin or dropping the stack
commonMistakes.text: Half-inserted pin or dropping the stack. Why: pin can slip; dropping removes control. Fix: push the pin in and lower the stack gently.

commonMistakes.title: Rolling the shoulders forward into the neck
commonMistakes.text: Rolling the shoulders forward into the neck. Why: crunches the shoulders and does not work the back. Fix: shoulders down and open.

safetyNotes: Pin and weights: push the weight-stack pin all the way in and check it before starting.
Light load first: rear delts and rotator cuff muscles are small; heavy loads lead to shrugging and swinging. If you cannot pause for one second at the end of a rep, it is too heavy.
Do not over-sweep: do not drive the arms far behind the shoulder line; stop at about shoulder level.
Shoulder pain: stop with sharp or pinching pain; if pain lasts over 2 weeks, see a clinician.
High blood pressure: breathe continuously; stop 2-3 reps short of failure.
Spotter: not needed on a machine; if you cannot finish a rep, bring the handles slowly to the start.

Gym etiquette: wipe the pad and handles; do not leave the pin at a heavy load; do not hog the machine between sets (the pec deck and the rear-delt machine are often the same machine); do not film other members.
